mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases consumer and business spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS remains low but SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises above 8.5% but SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) is strong but unemployment (UNRATE) is high, it indicates labor market inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as productivity may suffer.
failure_condition: If the combination of strong PAYEMS and high UNRATE occurs but SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings may decline.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is negative but SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as companies experience increased revenues.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth is positive but SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals reduced demand in the housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as related industries may struggle.
failure_condition: If HOUST falls below 700 but SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) alongside rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates tight monetary conditions and economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise but SPX 20-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDP (GDPC1) indicates reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings and consumer spending decline.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is negative but SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time.
